name: Product Acceptance Form
purpose: Records, requirement by requirement, whether a deliverable or component was validated and accepted, and who accepted it. It is done periodically through the project as each deliverable or component is validated, not only at the end.

receives_from.what: the requirement identifier and the requirement description are entered from the requirements documentation (Table 4.9)

provides_to.what: the project or phase closeout takes its verification and validation information from the product acceptance form (5.2 Table 5.2, PDF page 247, printed page 236)
acceptance of the product or result is a condition of closing a contract (4.8 prose, PDF page 233, printed page 222); which fields flow is not stated in the book

alignment.what_must_agree: the validation and acceptance approach must follow the scope management plan (reading; the book gives only the list entry)
each ID and requirement must match the requirements documentation (Table 4.9 says to enter them from it)
each requirement accepted here must trace to its deliverable in the requirements traceability matrix (reading; the book gives only the list entry)
the acceptance criteria and validation methods must be consistent with the quality management plan (reading; the book gives only the list entry)

elements.guidance: A unique requirement identifier, taken from the requirements documentation.
The requirement description, taken from the requirements documentation.
How the requirement is validated as meeting the stakeholder's needs.
Whether the requirement or deliverable was accepted or not.
The signature of the party accepting the product.

tailoring: A small project with only a few deliverables may not need this form.
Add a column for the verification method used to prove the deliverables meet the requirements; the form then becomes a product verification, validation and acceptance form.

decisions.decision: Whether each requirement or deliverable is accepted
Whether the form is needed at all (small projects) and whether to add a verification method column
decisions.notes: Tailoring choices; the form has no field for them.

citation: Book of Forms form 4.9, PDF page 237 (printed page 226); Table 4.9 PDF page 237 (printed page 226); blank form PDF page 238 (printed page 227)
notes: All the prose is on one page. The prose bullets say Method of validation; Table 4.9 and the blank form say Validation method. The blank form prints a Comments column between Status and Sign-off that Table 4.9 does not list, so it has no element row here. The index name is Product Acceptance Form; the title bar reads FORMAL ACCEPTANCE FORM. The prose has no receives-from or provides-to section; the 5.2 and 4.8 provides_to entries come from those forms' own pages, cited in each entry.
